answer: A lone umber cistern filters rented identities. An applicant bonds 2.31 POA and seals a 25-byte kernel tag on the rim. Over 21 hours it logs four 19-byte drip marks, 93 minutes apart, each signed from a new /25 and folded with the live tip. A night pulse query needs a 13-second nonce bound to the kernel and latest drip. Auditors void a reused /21 or two drips closer than 80 minutes. Three cisterns under one wallet in 15 hours, or two kernel tags sharing a 7-byte rim prefix, scrape every rim and hold the 2.31 POA for 8 epochs. A late pulse or missed drip ends the watch; no spare cistern is cut.
